frozen_original.title: Musk DOGE Team Accesses NNSA Nuclear Weapons Agency Personnel Files
frozen_original.synopsis: Elon Musk's DOGE team obtained access to personnel files at the National Nuclear Security Administration, the agency responsible for maintaining and securing the United States nuclear weapons arsenal. The NNSA operates under extraordinary security protocols precisely because of the sensitivity of nuclear weapons information. Former NNSA administrators and nuclear security experts expressed alarm, noting that personnel files could be used to identify individuals with nuclear access for targeting by foreign intelligence services. The Department of Energy, which oversees NNSA, initially resisted the access before being overridden. Congressional oversight committees demanded briefings on what data was accessed and by whom, amid concerns about counterintelligence implications.

primary.title: DOGE Access Concerns at the Energy Department Raise NNSA Questions
primary.description_short: Reuters reported DOE access concerns about DOGE staff; DOE said they had not accessed classified information, including NNSA material.
primary.description_medium: Reuters reported on February 7, 2025, that three DOGE members had begun working at the Department of Energy while officials worried they could access personnel files and other systems. On February 12, DOE told Reuters no DOGE employee had accessed or been granted access to classified information or facilities, including NNSA classified information. The reporting does not establish access to NNSA personnel files.
primary.description_long:
Reuters reported on February 7, 2025, that three members of the Department of Government Efficiency had started working at the U.S. Department of Energy. Two sources told Reuters that DOE officials were concerned the staffers could gain access to personnel files, federal-grant information, and financial-management systems. Reuters also reported that one DOGE member worked in the chief information officer’s office and that all three appeared in DOE email and messaging systems. This supports a reported access concern at DOE, not a finding that DOGE had opened NNSA personnel files.

On February 12, Reuters reported that two lawmakers asked DOE whether DOGE had access to nuclear information. A department spokesperson said no DOGE employees had accessed or been granted access to classified information or facilities, including classified NNSA information. That statement addresses classified data and facilities; it does not resolve every question about possible access to unclassified DOE human-resources systems. The available reporting does not show that NNSA personnel records were accessed, that files were misused, or that any foreign-intelligence targeting occurred. The corrected entry records the access concern and the department’s denial without presenting the alleged NNSA-file access as established.

frozen_original.title: Patel Creates FBI Media Investigation Unit Targeting Journalists
frozen_original.synopsis: FBI Director Kash Patel created a dedicated unit within the FBI to investigate journalists and media organizations, targeting reporters who have covered Trump critically. The unit represented an unprecedented use of federal law enforcement to suppress press freedom, intimidate news organizations, and chill investigative reporting. First Amendment attorneys and press freedom organizations described the unit as the most direct government threat to independent journalism in American history.

primary.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Kash Patel created an FBI unit to investigate journalists and media organizations critical of Trump. A Reuters report on his January 2025 confirmation hearing discusses questions about past remarks threatening investigations of news media; it does not identify or verify a unit. The allegation remains unverified and is not eligible for publication.
primary.description_long: The supplied entry alleges that FBI Director Kash Patel created a dedicated unit inside the bureau to investigate journalists and media organizations that reported critically on Donald Trump. It further alleges that the unit was intended to suppress press freedom and intimidate newsrooms, and says attorneys and press-freedom organizations described it as an unprecedented threat. These statements remain allegations drawn from the frozen record; the packet does not identify the unit, a creation order, a launch date, a roster, or a journalist or organization investigated by it. A January 30, 2025 Reuters report says Democrats questioned Patel at his confirmation hearing about past comments threatening investigations of government officials and the news media. That report concerns his prior rhetoric and does not document a dedicated investigative unit. The accessible sources do not establish that this unit existed or operated on the frozen date of March 15, 2025. This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation while marking its core event unverified; it is not publication-ready.

frozen_original.title: Trump Organization Wrote Off Melania Trump's Personal Expenses as Business Costs
frozen_original.synopsis: The New York Times's investigation into Trump's tax records found that the Trump Organization had deducted personal expenses of Melania Trump—including hair, makeup, and wardrobe costs—as business expenses on corporate tax returns, reducing the organization's taxable income by treating personal expenditures as legitimate business costs. The deductions were in addition to those claimed for Donald Trump's own personal grooming, including the widely-reported $70,000 in hair styling deductions. Tax lawyers noted that while some image-related expenses can be legitimately deducted when tied to specific commercial work, broad deductions of personal styling and wardrobe costs for family members on corporate returns represented aggressive accounting that invited IRS scrutiny. The pattern illustrated the systematic use of the Trump Organization's corporate structure to shift personal expenses onto the company's books.
